OpsFlow Backend — الدليل التعليمي الكامل

شرح باللهجة المصرية مبني على الملفات الموجودة في المستودع يوم 2026-10-15. كل ملف C# مشمول كاملًا ومعه تعليق بجانب كل سطر. افتح الأقسام اللي بتذاكرها؛ مش مطلوب تقرأ آلاف السطور مرة واحدة.

الـFrontend مستبعد. Entities وDbContext والـmigrations مستبعدة بطلبك. إعدادات التشغيل والاختبارات والـbenchmark والـdeployment مضمنة. القيم الشبيهة بالأسرار محجوبة.

5مشاريع تشغيل أساسية
2مشروعا tests في solution
133ملف C# مشمول
185ملف كود/تشغيل مضمن
طريقة المذاكرة: ابدأ بالفلوهات، ثم افتح ملفًا واحدًا في كل مرة وابحث عن اسم class. التعليق السطري يشرح تركيب اللغة، وبطاقة الملف وشرح الفلو يشرحان المقصود في التطبيق.
تنبيه: وجود Kubernetes/Terraform/CI config لا يثبت نشرًا فعليًا. لا توجد هنا أرقام أداء أو سعة مخترعة.

١) الصورة الكبيرة

الـAPI تستقبل HTTP؛ Application تنفذ حالة الاستخدام؛ Domain تحمل قواعد المجال؛ Infrastructure تنفذ الوصول للتخزين والأنظمة الخارجية. Worker عملية ثانية تستهلك الرسائل.

HTTP Client→API Controller→Application Service→Domain rules→Repository interface→Infrastructure→Postgres / Redis / RabbitMQ
Rabbit queue→Worker→log / retry / ack

المشاريع الخمسة

  • OpsFlow.Api: HTTP controllers وmiddleware وتشغيل الـhost.
  • OpsFlow.Application: services، DTOs، interfaces، mappings، settings.
  • OpsFlow.Domain: قواعد وأسماء المجال وinterfaces وenums/state machine. entities مستثناة.
  • OpsFlow.Infrastructure: adapters لقاعدة البيانات وRedis وRabbit وauth.
  • OpsFlow.Worker: مستهلك الرسائل بالخلفية.

الاختبارات والأدوات

  • UnitTests وIntegrationTests داخل solution.
  • RedisBenchmarkHost منفصل عن solution/runtime.
  • LoadTests بها k6 وPowerShell ونتائج محفوظة.

٢) المصطلحات الأساسية

Controller: يستقبل HTTP ويرجع response.
DTO: شكل البيانات المتبادلة مع API وليس جدول DB.
Service/use case: ينفذ قواعد العملية ويرتب الاستدعاءات.
Interface: عقد يحدد العمليات دون التنفيذ.
Repository: محول قراءة/كتابة بيانات المجال.
DI: container ينشئ dependencies ويمررها للـconstructor.
Scoped: نسخة ضمن request غالبًا.
Middleware: خطوة مشتركة في مسار الطلب.
JWT: access token موقّع يحمل claims.
Refresh token: قيمة عشوائية قابلة للإبطال والتدوير.
Cache: نسخة مؤقتة لقراءات متكررة.
Queue: وسيط يحتفظ برسالة حتى يستهلكها worker.

٣) DI وتشغيل الطلب

  1. بداية API في Program.cs؛ والـWorker له Program مستقل.
  2. مشروعا Application وInfrastructure يسجلان الخدمات في DependencyInjection.cs.
  3. الـController يأخذ الخدمات عبر constructor injection بدل إنشائها بنفسه.
  4. DI يربط الواجهة بالتنفيذ؛ مثل IIncidentService مع IncidentService.
ترتيب الـpipeline: Authentication يبني هوية من token، وبعده Authorization يقرر الصلاحيات؛ لذلك الترتيب مهم.

٤) Authentication خطوة خطوة

POST /api/auth/registerتسجيل إداري محمي.
POST /api/auth/self-registerمجهول في Development مع PublicRegistration مفعّل بحسب الكود.
POST /api/auth/loginemail/password ثم access + refresh عند النجاح.
POST /api/auth/refresh-tokenالتحقق ثم تدوير refresh token.
POST /api/auth/revoke-tokenإبطال refresh بعد التحقق من المالك والحالة.
  1. AuthController يستقبل DTO ويستدعي IAuthService.
  2. AuthService يطبّع البريد ويفحص التكرار/الدور/المؤسسة، ثم يخزن BCrypt hash لا كلمة المرور.
  3. Login يفحص المستخدم وحالته وBCrypt.Verify، ثم يطلب إنشاء access JWT وrefresh عشوائي ويحفظ refresh.
  4. JWT يحمل claims مثل معرف المستخدم والبريد والدور والمؤسسة وjti، وموقّع بمفتاح. Bearer middleware يتحقق من التوقيع والانتهاء والجهة والجمهور.
  5. Refresh يفحص وجود token وصلاحيته وربطه بالمستخدم، ثم يبطل/يدوّر القديم ويصدر بديلًا.
  6. Authorize attributes تحدد أدوارًا؛ بعض عمليات الخدمة تتحقق أيضًا من المؤسسة/المالك. 401 لا توجد هوية صالحة، 403 الهوية موجودة لكن غير مسموح.
مهم: refresh token ليس JWT. JWT access موقّع وقصير العمر؛ refresh قيمة محفوظة يمكن إبطالها. لا تضع secret حقيقي في Git.

الأدوار المعرفة: Admin، TeamLead، Engineer، Viewer؛ constants تقلل أخطاء الكتابة، لكن الصلاحية الفعلية تظهر في attributes والمنطق.

٥) Incident workflow

  1. IncidentsController يأخذ DTO وclaims ثم ينادي IIncidentService.
  2. IncidentService يتحقق من المؤسسة ونطاق الخدمة والصلاحية لمنع عبور بيانات مؤسسة أخرى.
  3. الإنشاء يبدأ بحالة Detected ويسجل timeline event ثم يحفظ ويكتب audit وينشر incidents.created.
  4. IncidentStateMachine تسمح بالانتقالات المعرفة: Detected→Investigating؛ Investigating→Identified أو Mitigating؛ Identified→Mitigating؛ Resolved→Postmortem أو Closed؛ Postmortem→Closed.
  5. Mitigating لا تخرج بانتقال عادي وفق الجدول؛ Resolve عملية مخصصة لتسجيل الحل والوقت.
  6. الخدمات تشمل assign/comments/timeline/severity/postmortem/reopen؛ DTO وcontroller والخدمة توضح تفاصيلها.
  7. بعض التعديلات تسجل audit وتنشر حدثًا.
حد معماري: حفظ PostgreSQL ونشر Rabbit عمليتان منفصلتان؛ لا يظهر Transactional Outbox، فلا تقل إنهما transaction واحدة.

٦) Redis

ServiceManagementService.GetByOrganizationAsync يقرأ قائمة services حسب organization. المفتاح services:org:{organizationId}، والـTTL الافتراضي 5 دقائق.

GET list→Redis key→hit: DTOs→miss: Postgres→map ثم cache
  • CacheKeys يبني المفتاح، وRedisCacheService يقرأ/يكتب JSON وينفذ expiration.
  • إنشاء/تعديل/حذف/تغيير حالة service يمسح key المؤسسة.
  • الـcache قد يصبح stale عند سباق القراءة والكتابة؛ TTL يقلل مدة بقائه ولا يضمن consistency لحظية.
  • لا تنشر نسبة تسريع دون benchmark موثق.

٧) RabbitMQ

  1. IncidentService ينادي IMessagePublisher في العمليات المحددة.
  2. RabbitMqPublisher ينشر JSON persistent إلى topic exchange opsflow.events بمفاتيح incidents.created وincidents.status_changed.
  3. Topology تربط queue durable/quorum باسم opsflow.notifications وتعرّف DLX/DLQ.
  4. OpsFlow.Worker يتصل بالـbroker ويقرأ برسائل manual ack وprefetch 1 حسب المصدر.
  5. المعالجة الحالية تسجل notification في log؛ لا تثبت إرسال email/SMS/webhook.
  6. الفشل يعيد نشر مع retry metadata، وبعد حد retries ينتهي إلى DLQ؛ فشل نقل الرسالة له nack/requeue حسب الكود.
محدودية: dedupe في ذاكرة process فقط وتمحى مع restart. Integration tests تستبدل publisher بـNoOp فلا تختبر Rabbit الحقيقي أو retry/DLQ end-to-end.

٨) الاختبارات

  • xUnit، Moq، FluentAssertions؛ Testcontainers وWebApplicationFactory لتكامل API مع Postgres مؤقت.
  • Unit tests تغطي AuthService وIncidentService/StateMachine وOrganizationService.
  • Integration tests تغطي login/token lifecycle و401/403 وبعض incident workflow عبر HTTP.
  • ناشر الرسائل NoOp في الاختبارات؛ Rabbit غير مختبر من هذا المسار.
  • لم أشغل الاختبارات لإعداد هذا الملف. الأمر: dotnet test OpsFlow.sln. وجود اختبار ليس نتيجة تشغيل.

٩) Benchmark والقياسات

ملفات Redis A/B وRedisBenchmarkHost وCompose معزول ونتائج CSV مضمنة أدناه. راجع README لفهم المنافذ والبيانات والتكرارات. قياس محلي لا يساوي سعة production؛ latency reduction تختلف عن throughput.

١٠) Docker وKubernetes وTerraform وCI

Compose

يربط حاويات التطوير API/Worker/Postgres/Redis/Rabbit؛ لا يثبت جاهزية production.

Kubernetes

YAML يصف موارد التطبيق والتخزين والإعداد؛ وجود الملف لا يثبت نشره.

Terraform

تعريف AWS network/EKS/ECR حسب deploy README؛ لا يثبت apply.

GitHub Actions

workflow يصف restore/test/scan/build/publish؛ OIDC/IAM والنجاح يحتاجان تحققًا منفصلًا.

تقنيات الاستخدام الظاهر: .NET 8/ASP.NET Core، EF Core مع Npgsql/PostgreSQL، StackExchange.Redis، RabbitMQ، JWT Bearer، BCrypt، xUnit/Moq/FluentAssertions/Testcontainers وk6. وجود package وحده ليس إثبات استخدام.

١١) ادعاءات مقابلة دقيقة

  • Backend مقسوم إلى API/Application/Domain/Infrastructure ومعه Worker.
  • JWT access وrefresh rotation مدعوم من AuthService وgenerator.
  • Redis لقائمة الخدمات حسب المؤسسة مع TTL وإبطال عند الكتابة؛ لا تدع رقم تسريع دون دليل.
  • Rabbit publisher/worker مع retry/DLQ، لكن worker يسجل notification وdedupe مؤقت.
  • قل «ملفات Kubernetes/Terraform/CI موجودة» بدل «نشرت production» بلا دليل.
  • لا تدع users capacity أو HA أو exactly-once دون قياس وتصميم يثبت ذلك.

١٢) خطة مذاكرة يومين

اليوم الأول

  1. Program.cs وmiddleware.
  2. AuthController → IAuthService → AuthService → JwtTokenGenerator.
  3. اتبع endpoint من IncidentsController إلى IncidentService.
  4. اقرأ StateMachine وDTOs والاختبار المقابل.

اليوم الثاني

  1. ServiceManagementService وRedisCacheService.
  2. IncidentService → Publisher → topology → Worker.
  3. افهم ack/retry وما لا تختبره IntegrationTestFactory.
  4. راجع Compose/Dockerfiles ثم K8s/Terraform/CI كتكوينات.
تدريب مقابلة: لكل endpoint جاوب: مين استقبل؟ مين طبق القواعد؟ مين قرأ/كتب؟ إيه الرد؟ وإيه حالات الفشل؟

١٣) ملفات الكود والإعداد الموجودة في الدليل

C# المشمول: 133 (runtime 122، tests/tools 11). مستبعد 12 entity و6 ملفات DbContext/migration/snapshot. Frontend غير مضمّن. ملفات C# كاملة ومشروحة سطرًا بسطر.

الملف كاملًا؛ القيم السرية محجوبة
name: CI and CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install .NET 8 SDK
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: 8.0.x

      - name: Restore dependencies
        run: dotnet restore OpsFlow.sln

      - name: Build and run tests
        run: dotnet test OpsFlow.sln --no-restore --configuration Release

  security-scan:
    name: Scan source dependencies and configuration
    needs: build-and-test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install .NET 8 SDK
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: 8.0.x

      - name: Restore dependencies for scanning
        run: dotnet restore OpsFlow.sln

      - name: Scan filesystem with Trivy
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: .
          scanners: vuln,misconfig
          severity: CRITICAL
          ignore-unfixed: true
          exit-code: '1'

  docker-build:
    name: Build and scan Docker images
    needs: security-scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build API image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: OpsFlow.Api/Dockerfile
          load: true
          tags: opsflow-api:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Build Worker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: OpsFlow.Worker/Dockerfile
          load: true
          tags: opsflow-worker:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Scan API image with Trivy
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: image
          image-ref: opsflow-api:${{ github.sha }}
          severity: CRITICAL
          ignore-unfixed: true
          exit-code: '1'

      - name: Scan Worker image with Trivy
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: image
          image-ref: opsflow-worker:${{ github.sha }}
          severity: CRITICAL
          ignore-unfixed: true
          exit-code: '1'

  push-to-ecr:
    name: Publish images to Amazon ECR
    needs: docker-build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    env:
      AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME: ${{ vars.AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME }}
      ECR_REPOSITORY_API: ${{ vars.ECR_REPOSITORY_API }}
      ECR_REPOSITORY_WORKER: ${{ vars.ECR_REPOSITORY_WORKER }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check required ECR configuration
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for name in AWS_REGION AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME ECR_REPOSITORY_API ECR_REPOSITORY_WORKER; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              echo "Missing GitHub Actions variable: ${name}"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - name: Configure AWS credentials with GitHub OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6.3.0
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to Amazon ECR
        id: ecr
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Publish API image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: OpsFlow.Api/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ steps.ecr.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY_API }}:${{ github.sha }}
            ${{ steps.ecr.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY_API }}:latest

      - name: Publish Worker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: OpsFlow.Worker/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ steps.ecr.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY_WORKER }}:${{ github.sha }}
            ${{ steps.ecr.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY_WORKER }}:latest

# Optional public entry point. Keep out of kustomization.yaml.
# Before applying: replace the ACM certificate ARN and rotate/remove the
# demo credentials seeded by OpsFlowDbSeeder in an application change.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: opsflow-api-public
  namespace: opsflow
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: internet-facing
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type: ip
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/REPLACE-ME
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports: "443"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: HTTP
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-path: /api/health
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-api
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: http
      protocol: TCP

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: opsflow-api
  namespace: opsflow
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-api
spec:
  # Start with one replica because the API applies database migrations and
  # seeds the first organization during startup.
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-api
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      initContainers:
        - name: wait-for-dependencies
          image: busybox:1.36.1
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - until nc -z postgres 5432 && nc -z redis 6379 && nc -z rabbitmq 5672; do echo 'waiting for OpsFlow dependencies'; sleep 2; done
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 10m
              memory: 16Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 64Mi
      containers:
        - name: api
          # Replace this image with the API ECR URL and an immutable commit tag.
          image: opsflow-api:replace-before-deploy
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: opsflow-config
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: POSTGRES_USER
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
            - name: REDIS_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: REDIS_PASSWORD
            - name: RABBITMQ_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: RABBITMQ_USER
            - name: RabbitMq__UserName
              value: "$(RABBITMQ_USER)"
            - name: RabbitMq__Password
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
            - name: ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection
              value: "Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=$(POSTGRES_DB);Username=$(POSTGRES_USER);Password=[REDACTED];"
            - name: Redis__ConnectionString
              value: "redis:6379,password=[REDACTED]"
            - name: JwtSettings__SecretKey
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: JWT_SECRET_KEY
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 150m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 1Gi
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /api/health
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 30
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /api/health
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 3
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /api/health
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 20
            failureThreshold: 3
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: opsflow-api
  namespace: opsflow
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-api
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8080
      targetPort: http
      protocol: TCP

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: opsflow-config
  namespace: opsflow
data:
  ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Production"
  ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS: "8080"
  POSTGRES_DB: "opsflow_db"
  RabbitMq__HostName: "rabbitmq"
  RabbitMq__Port: "5672"
  RabbitMq__VirtualHost: "/"
  RabbitMq__Exchange: "opsflow.events"
  RabbitMq__Queue: "opsflow.notifications"
  RabbitMq__DeadLetterExchange: "opsflow.events.dlx"
  RabbitMq__DeadLetterQueue: "opsflow.notifications.dlq"
  RabbitMq__MaxDeliveryAttempts: "3"
  JwtSettings__Issuer: "OpsFlow"
  JwtSettings__Audience: "OpsFlowClients"
  JwtSettings__AccessTokenExpirationMinutes: "60"
  JwtSettings__RefreshTokenExpirationDays: "7"

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: opsflow
resources:

kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: opsflow

  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres
  ports:
    - name: postgres
      port: 5432
      targetPort: 5432

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: opsflow
spec:
  serviceName: postgres-headless
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16-alpine
          ports:
            - name: postgres
              containerPort: 5432
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-config
                  key: POSTGRES_DB
            - name: POSTGRES_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: POSTGRES_USER
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
            - name: PGDATA
              value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 1Gi
          startupProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - pg_isready -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 30
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - pg_isready -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 3
          livenessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - pg_isready -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 20
            failureThreshold: 3
          volumeMounts:
            - name: postgres-data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: postgres-data
      spec:
        accessModes:
          - ReadWriteOnce
        storageClassName: opsflow-gp3
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 8Gi

apiVersion: apps/v1

                  key: RABBITMQ_USER

              valueFrom:

                  key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD

            failureThreshold: 3
          livenessProbe:

                - rabbitmq-diagnostics
                - -q

  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: rabbitmq-data
      spec:

        resources:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redis
  namespace: opsflow
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: redis
          image: redis:7-alpine
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - exec redis-server --save "" --appendonly no --requirepass "$REDIS_PASSWORD"
          ports:
            - name: redis
              containerPort: 6379
          env:
            - name: REDIS_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: REDIS_PASSWORD
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
          startupProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping | grep -q PONG
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 30
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping | grep -q PONG
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping | grep -q PONG
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 20

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: opsflow-worker
  namespace: opsflow
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-worker
spec:
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-worker
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: opsflow-worker
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      initContainers:
        - name: wait-for-rabbitmq
          image: busybox:1.36.1
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - until nc -z rabbitmq 5672; do echo 'waiting for RabbitMQ'; sleep 2; done
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 10m
              memory: 16Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 64Mi
      containers:
        - name: worker
          # Replace this image with the Worker ECR URL and an immutable commit tag.
          image: opsflow-worker:replace-before-deploy
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: opsflow-config
          env:
            - name: RABBITMQ_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: RABBITMQ_USER
            - name: RabbitMq__UserName
              value: "$(RABBITMQ_USER)"
            - name: RabbitMq__Password
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: opsflow-runtime-secrets
                  key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi

# OpsFlow on AWS: Kubernetes orchestration + Terraform

This folder describes a small, reproducible AWS deployment for the existing OpsFlow API and Worker. Terraform creates the AWS network, an EKS cluster using EKS Auto Mode, and two ECR image repositories. Kubernetes then runs the API, Worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ.

This is a learning/demo deployment, not a claim of production high availability. PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ each run as a single in-cluster StatefulSet with persistent EBS volumes; Redis is a single, non-persistent cache. There is no monitoring stack here. Kubernetes health probes are only used to decide whether a container should receive traffic or restart.

## What orchestration means here

Kubernetes keeps the declared workloads running and connects them through in-cluster Services. For example, the API addresses PostgreSQL as `postgres:5432`, Redis as `redis:6379`, and RabbitMQ as `rabbitmq:5672`; Kubernetes DNS resolves those names. Deployments manage the API, Worker, and Redis pods. StatefulSets and persistent volume claims are used for PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ. The API and Worker wait for dependencies to accept TCP connections before starting.

Terraform creates the AWS foundation that Kubernetes needs: a dedicated VPC with public/private subnets and NAT, EKS, and ECR. Terraform does not build or push application images, create application secrets, or deploy the Kubernetes manifests.

## Important safety notes

- No AWS resources were created by preparing these files. `terraform apply` is a separate, billable action that you run yourself.
- Limit the EKS public API endpoint to your current public IP as a `/32` in `cluster_admin_cidrs`; do not use `0.0.0.0/0`.
- Keep real credentials in a local `secrets.env` file and Kubernetes Secret. Never commit it.
- The current application seeder inserts known demo accounts when the database has no organizations (see `OpsFlow.Infrastructure/Data/OpsFlowDbSeeder.cs`). Do not expose this API publicly until those credentials are changed/removed through an application/data change.
- The API Service is `ClusterIP` by default. Test it with `kubectl port-forward`. An optional TLS/NLB example is provided separately and is not included in the default Kustomize deployment.
- The sample stores PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ data on EBS, but does not configure backups, multi-AZ database failover, or managed services. Deleting the cluster can delete its storage depending on the EBS/PVC lifecycle.

## Prerequisites

Install and authenticate the AWS CLI, Terraform, kubectl, and Docker. The AWS identity needs permissions for VPC, EKS, ECR, IAM roles/policies, and related resources. Terraform module/provider downloads require network access.

## 1. Configure and create AWS infrastructure

Run these commands in PowerShell from the repository root:

```powershell
Copy-Item deploy/terraform/aws/terraform.tfvars.example deploy/terraform/aws/terraform.tfvars
```

Edit `deploy/terraform/aws/terraform.tfvars`: set `cluster_admin_cidrs` to your public IPv4 address followed by `/32`, for example `198.51.100.24/32`. The value in the example file is reserved documentation IP space and must be replaced.

```powershell
Set-Location deploy/terraform/aws
terraform init
terraform fmt -check
terraform validate
terraform plan -out opsflow.tfplan
terraform apply opsflow.tfplan
```

Review the plan before applying. The cluster, EKS Auto Mode compute, NAT Gateway, and EBS volumes can incur AWS charges. Save the Terraform state: it records which cloud resources Terraform created.

Configure kubectl for the newly-created cluster:

```powershell
$cluster = terraform output -raw cluster_name
$region = terraform output -raw aws_region
aws eks update-kubeconfig --name $cluster --region $region
kubectl get nodes
```

Return to the repository root before building Docker images and applying the manifests:

```powershell
Set-Location ..\..\..
```

## 2. Build and push the two application images

The image definitions are `OpsFlow.Api/Dockerfile` and `OpsFlow.Worker/Dockerfile`. Use the ECR URLs created by Terraform and an immutable source revision tag:

```powershell
$apiRepo = terraform -chdir=deploy/terraform/aws output -raw api_ecr_repository_url
$workerRepo = terraform -chdir=deploy/terraform/aws output -raw worker_ecr_repository_url
$accountId = (aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
$region = terraform -chdir=deploy/terraform/aws output -raw aws_region
$tag = (git rev-parse --short HEAD)
aws ecr get-login-password --region $region | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$accountId.dkr.ecr.$region.amazonaws.com"
docker build -f OpsFlow.Api/Dockerfile -t "${apiRepo}:$tag" .
docker push "${apiRepo}:$tag"
docker build -f OpsFlow.Worker/Dockerfile -t "${workerRepo}:$tag" .
docker push "${workerRepo}:$tag"
```

Replace the placeholder `image:` values in `deploy/kubernetes/api.yaml` and `deploy/kubernetes/worker.yaml` with the respective ECR URL and the same `$tag`, such as `123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/opsflow-demo-api:abc1234`.

## 3. Create runtime secrets and deploy Kubernetes resources

Copy the template and replace every value with unique generated values. Use passwords consisting of letters/numbers because the app's Redis connection string is assembled from a password value.

```powershell
Copy-Item deploy/kubernetes/secrets.env.example deploy/kubernetes/secrets.env
notepad deploy/kubernetes/secrets.env
kubectl apply -f deploy/kubernetes/namespace.yaml
kubectl create secret generic opsflow-runtime-secrets `
  --namespace opsflow `
  --from-env-file deploy/kubernetes/secrets.env `
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl apply -k deploy/kubernetes
```

`JWT_SECRET_KEY` must contain at least 32 random characters. The Postgres, Redis, and RabbitMQ credentials must match between the Secret and their workloads; the manifests wire these values into the containers. Keep `secrets.env` local.

The API calls EF Core migrations and the demo seeder at startup. It is intentionally configured with one replica to avoid multiple API pods trying to initialize/seed the same empty database at once. The current seeder includes demo user accounts; review `OpsFlow.Infrastructure/Data/OpsFlowDbSeeder.cs` before any real/public deployment.

Check Kubernetes rollout state:

```powershell
kubectl get pods,services,pvc -n opsflow
kubectl rollout status deployment/opsflow-api -n opsflow
kubectl rollout status deployment/opsflow-worker -n opsflow
```

The API Service is private to the cluster. To test from your machine without making it public:

```powershell
kubectl port-forward service/opsflow-api 8080:8080 -n opsflow
```

In a second terminal, call the health endpoint:

```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:8080/api/health
```

## Optional public HTTPS entry point

`deploy/kubernetes/api-public-service.example.yaml` is deliberately excluded from `kustomization.yaml`. It demonstrates an internet-facing AWS Network Load Balancer with TLS termination using an ACM certificate. Replace the certificate ARN with a certificate in the same AWS region, configure DNS, and apply only after the demo credentials have been rotated/removed and the application has been reviewed for public use:

```powershell
kubectl apply -f deploy/kubernetes/api-public-service.example.yaml
kubectl get service opsflow-api-public -n opsflow
```

EKS Auto Mode provisions a load balancer for a `LoadBalancer` Service. This example does not create an ACM certificate or DNS record.

## Cleanup

Delete application workloads first, then destroy AWS resources from the Terraform directory:

```powershell
kubectl delete -k deploy/kubernetes
Set-Location deploy/terraform/aws
terraform destroy
```

Review the destroy plan. Confirm that any data you need has been backed up before deleting persistent storage. Keep the Terraform state until the destroy finishes successfully; deleting state first would make resource cleanup harder. ECR images and AWS resources may have separate lifecycle/billing implications, so verify the resulting AWS account state after cleanup.

## File map

- `terraform/aws/*.tf`: AWS provider, network, EKS Auto Mode, ECR, outputs, and configurable inputs.
- `kubernetes/kustomization.yaml`: default application deployment bundle.
- `kubernetes/api.yaml`, `worker.yaml`: application Deployments and internal API Service.
- `kubernetes/postgres.yaml`, `rabbitmq.yaml`: single-replica StatefulSets and persistent claims.
- `kubernetes/redis.yaml`: single Redis cache Deployment.
- `kubernetes/configmap.yaml`, `secrets.env.example`: non-secret settings and local secret template.
- `kubernetes/storage.yaml`: encrypted `gp3` EBS StorageClass for EKS Auto Mode.
- `kubernetes/api-public-service.example.yaml`: optional public TLS entry point; not applied by default.

data "aws_availability_zones" "available" {
  state = "available"
}

locals {
  name = "${var.project_name}-${var.environment}"
  azs  = slice(data.aws_availability_zones.available.names, 0, 2)
}

module "vpc" {
  source  = "terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws"
  version = "6.7.3"

  name = local.name
  cidr = var.vpc_cidr

  azs             = local.azs
  private_subnets = [cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 8, 1), cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 8, 2)]
  public_subnets  = [cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 8, 101), cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 8, 102)]

  enable_dns_hostnames = true
  enable_dns_support   = true

  # A single NAT gateway keeps this sample smaller than one NAT per AZ.
  # EKS nodes use private subnets; public load balancers use public subnets.
  enable_nat_gateway = true
  single_nat_gateway = true

  public_subnet_tags = {
    "kubernetes.io/role/elb"                  = "1"
    "kubernetes.io/cluster/${local.name}"     = "shared"
  }

  private_subnet_tags = {
    "kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb"         = "1"
    "kubernetes.io/cluster/${local.name}"     = "shared"
    "karpenter.sh/discovery"                  = local.name
  }
}

module "eks" {
  source  = "terraform-aws-modules/eks/aws"
  version = "21.26.0"

  name               = local.name
  kubernetes_version = var.kubernetes_version

  vpc_id                   = module.vpc.vpc_id
  subnet_ids               = module.vpc.private_subnets
  control_plane_subnet_ids = module.vpc.private_subnets

  endpoint_public_access  = true
  endpoint_private_access = true
  endpoint_public_access_cidrs = var.cluster_admin_cidrs

  enable_cluster_creator_admin_permissions = true

  # EKS Auto Mode manages workload compute, EBS-backed storage,
  # pod networking, and Service type=LoadBalancer integration.
  compute_config = {
    enabled    = true
    node_pools = ["general-purpose", "system"]
  }

  tags = {
    Project     = var.project_name
    Environment = var.environment
  }
}

resource "aws_ecr_repository" "api" {
  name                 = "${local.name}-api"
  image_tag_mutability = "MUTABLE"

  image_scanning_configuration {
    scan_on_push = true
  }
}

resource "aws_ecr_repository" "worker" {
  name                 = "${local.name}-worker"
  image_tag_mutability = "MUTABLE"

  image_scanning_configuration {
    scan_on_push = true
  }
}

resource "aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy" "api" {
  repository = aws_ecr_repository.api.name

  policy = jsonencode({
    rules = [{
      rulePriority = 1
      description  = "Expire untagged API images after 14 days"
      selection = {
        tagStatus   = "untagged"
        countType   = "sinceImagePushed"
        countUnit   = "days"
        countNumber = 14
      }
      action = { type = "expire" }
    }]
  })
}

resource "aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy" "worker" {
  repository = aws_ecr_repository.worker.name

  policy = jsonencode({
    rules = [{
      rulePriority = 1
      description  = "Expire untagged Worker images after 14 days"
      selection = {
        tagStatus   = "untagged"
        countType   = "sinceImagePushed"
        countUnit   = "days"
        countNumber = 14
      }
      action = { type = "expire" }
    }]
  })
}

  default     = "opsflow"
}

variable "environment" {
  description = "Environment suffix used in AWS resource names and tags."
  type        = string
  default     = "demo"
}

variable "kubernetes_version" {
  description = "Amazon EKS Kubernetes minor version. Update when upgrading the cluster."
  type        = string
  default     = "1.35"
}

variable "vpc_cidr" {
  description = "CIDR range for the dedicated OpsFlow VPC."
  type        = string
  default     = "10.40.0.0/16"
}

variable "cluster_admin_cidrs" {
  description = "Public IPv4 CIDR ranges allowed to reach the EKS Kubernetes API endpoint. Set this to your current public IP as /32."
  type        = list(string)

  validation {
    condition     = length(var.cluster_admin_cidrs) > 0 && alltrue([for cidr in var.cluster_admin_cidrs : can(cidrhost(cidr, 0))])
    error_message = "Provide at least one valid CIDR range for EKS API access."
  }
}

وظيفته: Manifest/CI config؛ وجود الملف لا يثبت نشره أو نجاحه.
الملف كاملًا؛ القيم السرية محجوبة
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-opsflow_db}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-opsflow_user}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
    ports:
      - "${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5433}:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 10s

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${REDIS_HOST_PORT:-6380}:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:4-management
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # RabbitMQ's built-in guest account cannot connect from other containers.
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER: ${RABBITMQ_USER:-opsflow}
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS: ${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED]}
    ports:
      - "${RABBITMQ_HOST_PORT:-5673}:5672"
      - "${RABBITMQ_MANAGEMENT_HOST_PORT:-15673}:15672"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "rabbitmq-diagnostics", "-q", "check_port_connectivity"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 20s

  api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: OpsFlow.Api/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Development
      ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS: 8080
      ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection: "Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=${POSTGRES_DB:-opsflow_db};Username=${POSTGRES_USER:-opsflow_user};Password=[REDACTED];"
      Redis__ConnectionString: redis:6379
      RabbitMq__HostName: rabbitmq
      RabbitMq__Port: 5672
      RabbitMq__UserName: ${RABBITMQ_USER:-opsflow}
      RabbitMq__Password: ${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED]}
      # Local-development fallback only. Set JWT_SECRET_KEY outside development environments.
      JwtSettings__SecretKey: ${JWT_SECRET_KEY:-[REDACTED]}
    ports:
      - "${API_HOST_PORT:-5153}:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # The runtime image intentionally stays minimal; check that the API process is alive.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "kill -0 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  web:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: web/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${WEB_HOST_PORT:-5174}:80"
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy

  worker:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: OpsFlow.Worker/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      RabbitMq__HostName: rabbitmq
      RabbitMq__Port: 5672
      RabbitMq__UserName: ${RABBITMQ_USER:-opsflow}
      RabbitMq__Password: ${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED]}
    depends_on:
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres_data:

الملف كاملًا؛ القيم السرية محجوبة
# CI/CD pipeline

The GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml` runs on pushes to `main` and `master`, pull requests, and manual dispatches.

## What it does

1. Restores the solution, then builds and runs its tests on .NET 8.
2. Scans the repository's dependencies and configuration with Trivy. Unfixed Critical findings are ignored; other Critical findings fail the workflow.
3. Builds the API and Worker Docker images and scans both images for Critical vulnerabilities.
4. On a push to `main` only, authenticates to AWS through GitHub OIDC and publishes both images to ECR. Images receive the commit SHA tag and the `latest` tag.

The ECR publish job intentionally does not run on pull requests, manual dispatch, or `master` pushes. The repository currently uses `master`, so the first three jobs can run there; ECR publishing starts after the deployment branch is `main` and AWS is configured.

## Configure AWS ECR publishing

Create two ECR repositories, one for the API and one for the Worker. Configure GitHub repository **Actions variables** (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables):

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AWS_REGION` | AWS region containing the ECR repositories, such as `eu-west-1` |
| `AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME` | ARN of an IAM role configured for GitHub OIDC |
| `ECR_REPOSITORY_API` | ECR repository name for the API image |
| `ECR_REPOSITORY_WORKER` | ECR repository name for the Worker image |

The IAM role trust policy should use the GitHub OIDC provider, audience `sts.amazonaws.com`, and restrict the subject to this repository's `main` branch (`repo:mohamed19638/OpsFlow:ref:refs/heads/main`). Give the role only the ECR permissions required to obtain an authorization token and push image layers/manifests to the two repositories. Do not add AWS access keys to GitHub; OIDC issues short-lived credentials for the job. See [GitHub's AWS OIDC guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/security-harden-deployments/oidc-in-aws).

The workflow reports a clear error if an ECR variable is missing when the `main` publish job runs. AWS role trust, IAM permissions, and repository names still need to be configured in AWS/GitHub before the first image can publish.

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Copy project files first so Docker can reuse the restore layer when only source changes.
COPY OpsFlow.Domain/OpsFlow.Domain.csproj OpsFlow.Domain/
COPY OpsFlow.Application/OpsFlow.Application.csproj OpsFlow.Application/
COPY OpsFlow.Infrastructure/OpsFlow.Infrastructure.csproj OpsFlow.Infrastructure/
COPY OpsFlow.Api/OpsFlow.Api.csproj OpsFlow.Api/

RUN dotnet restore OpsFlow.Api/OpsFlow.Api.csproj

COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish OpsFlow.Api/OpsFlow.Api.csproj \
    --configuration Release \
    --output /app/publish \
    --no-restore

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS final
WORKDIR /app

ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080
EXPOSE 8080

COPY --from=build /app/publish .
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "OpsFlow.Api.dll"]

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Copy project files first so Docker can reuse the restore layer when only source changes.
COPY OpsFlow.Domain/OpsFlow.Domain.csproj OpsFlow.Domain/
COPY OpsFlow.Application/OpsFlow.Application.csproj OpsFlow.Application/
COPY OpsFlow.Infrastructure/OpsFlow.Infrastructure.csproj OpsFlow.Infrastructure/
COPY OpsFlow.Worker/OpsFlow.Worker.csproj OpsFlow.Worker/

RUN dotnet restore OpsFlow.Worker/OpsFlow.Worker.csproj

COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish OpsFlow.Worker/OpsFlow.Worker.csproj \
    --configuration Release \
    --output /app/publish \
    --no-restore

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:8.0 AS final
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=build /app/publish .
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "OpsFlow.Worker.dll"]

الملف كاملًا؛ القيم السرية محجوبة
import http from 'k6/http';
import { check } from 'k6';
import { Counter, Rate, Trend } from 'k6/metrics';
import encoding from 'k6/encoding';

const baseUrl = (__ENV.BASE_URL || 'http://host.docker.internal:5153').replace(/\/$/, '');
const email = __ENV.ADMIN_EMAIL || 'admin@acmetech.io';
const password = [REDACTED] || '[REDACTED DEVELOPMENT CREDENTIAL]';

const servicesRequests = new Counter('services_requests');
const servicesErrors = new Rate('services_errors');
const servicesLatency = new Trend('services_latency', true);
const incidentsRequests = new Counter('incidents_requests');
const incidentsErrors = new Rate('incidents_errors');
const incidentsLatency = new Trend('incidents_latency', true);
const createRequests = new Counter('create_incident_requests');
const createErrors = new Rate('create_incident_errors');
const createLatency = new Trend('create_incident_latency', true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    services_browse: { executor: 'constant-vus', exec: 'getServices', vus: 100, duration: '30s' },
    incidents_browse: { executor: 'constant-vus', exec: 'getIncidents', vus: 50, duration: '30s' },
    incident_create: { executor: 'constant-vus', exec: 'createIncident', vus: 10, duration: '30s' },
  },
  thresholds: {
    services_errors: ['rate<0.01'],
    incidents_errors: ['rate<0.01'],
    create_incident_errors: ['rate<0.01'],
  },
  summaryTrendStats: ['avg', 'min', 'med', 'max', 'p(50)', 'p(90)', 'p(95)', 'p(99)'],
};

export function setup() {
  const login = http.post(`${baseUrl}/api/auth/login`, JSON.stringify({ email, password }), {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
  check(login, { 'admin login succeeds': (response) => response.status === 200 });
  if (login.status !== 200) {
    throw new Error(`Admin login failed (${login.status}): ${login.body}`);
  }

  const accessToken = login.json('accessToken');
  const payload = JSON.parse(encoding.b64decode(accessToken.split('.')[1], 'rawurl', 's'));
  const organizationId = payload.orgId;
  const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` };
  const servicesResponse = http.get(`${baseUrl}/api/organizations/${organizationId}/services`, { headers });
  check(servicesResponse, { 'services setup request succeeds': (response) => response.status === 200 });
  if (servicesResponse.status !== 200) {
    throw new Error(`Loading services failed (${servicesResponse.status}): ${servicesResponse.body}`);
  }
  const services = servicesResponse.json();
  if (!services || services.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('The seeded organization has no services for the load test.');
  }

  return { accessToken, organizationId, serviceId: services[0].id };
}

export function getServices(data) {
  const response = http.get(`${baseUrl}/api/organizations/${data.organizationId}/services`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${data.accessToken}` },
    tags: { operation: 'services' },
  });
  servicesRequests.add(1);
  servicesErrors.add(response.status !== 200);
  servicesLatency.add(response.timings.duration);
  check(response, { 'GET services returns 200': (result) => result.status === 200 });
}

export function getIncidents(data) {
  const response = http.get(`${baseUrl}/api/organizations/${data.organizationId}/incidents`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${data.accessToken}` },
    tags: { operation: 'incidents' },
  });
  incidentsRequests.add(1);
  incidentsErrors.add(response.status !== 200);
  incidentsLatency.add(response.timings.duration);
  check(response, { 'GET incidents returns 200': (result) => result.status === 200 });
}

export function createIncident(data) {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({
    title: `k6 load test ${__VU}-${__ITER}`,
    description: 'Incident generated by the OpsFlow Phase 8 local load test.',
    severity: 'Low',
    serviceId: data.serviceId,
  });
  const response = http.post(`${baseUrl}/api/organizations/${data.organizationId}/incidents`, payload, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${data.accessToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    tags: { operation: 'create_incident' },
  });
  createRequests.add(1);
  createErrors.add(response.status !== 201);
  createLatency.add(response.timings.duration);
  check(response, { 'POST incident returns 201': (result) => result.status === 201 });
}

# Phase 8 load-test result

Run date: 2026-10-10. Target: a separate local Docker Compose stack with a newly created PostgreSQL volume, so generated incidents did not go into the existing development database. Load duration: 30 seconds per scenario, running concurrently; maximum configured concurrency: 160 VUs. k6 ran in the `grafana/k6:latest` Docker image.

| Operation | VUs | Requests | Requests/s | Errors | p50 | p95 | p99 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GET services | 100 | 17,235 | 549.96 | 0% | 143.47 ms | 415.68 ms | 592.46 ms |
| GET incidents | 50 | 3,832 | 122.28 | 0% | 266.37 ms | 1.12 s | 1.58 s |
| POST incident | 10 | 759 | 24.22 | 0% | 378.27 ms | 738.58 ms | 1.08 s |

The run completed all 21,826 scenario iterations (21,828 HTTP requests including setup) at an overall 696.51 requests/s and passed all three error-rate thresholds (less than 1%). The request rates and latencies describe this one local run; they are useful as a baseline, not a production capacity guarantee. Hardware, Docker resource limits, database size, and background services affect the numbers.

# OpsFlow Redis A/B benchmark

This benchmark uses the existing `ServicesController`, `ServiceManagementService`, repository, DTOs, JWT authentication and response. It adds a separate benchmark host and does not change the production API, existing load-test script, or existing test projects.

## Safety and scenarios

The Compose project is `opsflow-redis-benchmark`. It has its own PostgreSQL volume and Redis container, bound to loopback ports 15433 and 16380. Do not point this benchmark at the existing `opsflow` database or Redis. The seeded organization and service records are created once in this disposable database and remain unchanged during all three scenarios.

- **Bypass (A):** benchmark host replaces `ICacheService` with `BenchmarkBypassCacheService`. Each call behaves as a cache miss; reads still go to PostgreSQL and writes do nothing.
- **Miss (B):** benchmark host uses Redis. The runner removes `services:org:{orgId}` before each timed GET. The timed GET queries PostgreSQL and repopulates Redis.
- **Hit (C):** benchmark host uses Redis. The runner primes the key before timing, checks that the key exists, then measures requests whose logs show `Cache HIT`.

The PowerShell runner times only the HTTP GET, not cache deletion or prewarming. It compares status, response byte count and SHA-256 across scenarios and writes raw samples, per-run percentiles and host logs under `%TEMP%\OpsFlowRedisBenchmark\<run-id>`.

## Start the isolated dependencies

From the repository root in PowerShell:

```powershell
docker compose -p opsflow-redis-benchmark -f docker-compose.redis-benchmark.yml up -d postgres redis
docker compose -p opsflow-redis-benchmark -f docker-compose.redis-benchmark.yml ps
```

Confirm that this project lists only the benchmark PostgreSQL and Redis containers, with ports 15433 and 16380, before continuing. The API and Worker from the existing `opsflow` project are not used.

## Sequential latency run

The runner builds the benchmark host, starts it in Bypass or Redis mode, logs in with the seed admin, and performs 100 samples per scenario across 3 repetitions by default. It discards 5 warm-up requests per scenario. The order rotates between repetitions. Each B sample deletes the key before the timer starts; each C repetition explicitly primes it.

```powershell
.\tests\OpsFlow.LoadTests\redis-ab-sequential.ps1
```

The default seed login is present in `OpsFlowDbSeeder`; it is only for the disposable local benchmark database. Override `-AdminEmail` and `-AdminPassword` if the seed credentials change.

## Controlled k6 load runs

The wrapper builds and starts the benchmark host separately for A and C. Defaults are 25 virtual users, 30 seconds, and 3 repetitions for each scenario. It saves k6 JSON summaries and logs under `%TEMP%\OpsFlowRedisBenchmark\k6-<run-id>`. The exported summaries remove the login token. The setup login and warm-up request happen before the measured scenario.

```powershell
.\tests\OpsFlow.LoadTests\redis-ab-load.ps1
```

For a shorter pilot, use `-Vus 2 -Duration 5s -Repetitions 1`. The script checks that every response has the same body hash as setup, confirms the cache path from API logs, and records end-to-end latency percentiles, throughput and request failures. Keep the host logs to inspect EF command durations for database-backed requests.

There is one cache key for this organization. A cold-cache concurrent burst naturally includes a miss followed by hits as soon as the first request repopulates the key. Therefore scenario B is measured as repeated cold **single requests**, not misreported as a sustained all-miss load test. A and C receive steady-state controlled load tests.

## Interpreting and reporting results

Report p50, p95 and p99 for each repetition, errors, and k6 requests per second. Report median and range (or standard deviation) across repetitions. Compare the same statistic from A and C:

```text
latency reduction % = ((A latency - C latency) / A latency) * 100
latency speedup ratio = A latency / C latency
```

Use p50-to-p50 and p95-to-p95 comparisons. Latency reduction and throughput change are different measurements. Do not describe the result as a user-capacity figure or claim Redis reduced PostgreSQL load without query-count evidence from the same run.

Redis logs time the GET operation but stop before JSON deserialization; the existing service does not separately time Redis SET. EF Core command logs contain database command durations. These timings are diagnostic and should be reported separately from end-to-end HTTP latency. Keep host logs for each run so the path evidence is auditable.

## Results captured on 2026-10-14

These are local measurements from the isolated benchmark stack, one seeded organization with four services, one API process, PostgreSQL and Redis in local Docker, and the same 1,264-byte response body (same SHA-256 in every sequential sample). The machine model, CPU, memory and Docker resource limits were not captured, so these figures describe only this run and are not portable capacity claims.

### Sequential requests (100 samples per scenario, 3 repetitions)

The table shows the median of the three per-run percentiles. No request failed and all response hashes matched. The full 900 sequential samples and per-run summary rows are checked in under `tests/OpsFlow.LoadTests/results/2026-10-14/`.

| Scenario | p50 | p95 | p99 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PostgreSQL bypass | 5.105 ms | 7.563 ms | 8.352 ms |
| Redis cold miss + PostgreSQL + cache write | 11.777 ms | 17.668 ms | 19.741 ms |
| Redis hit | 5.208 ms | 7.481 ms | 8.097 ms |

Against bypass, the Redis-hit p50 was 2.02% slower (0.98x), p95 was 1.08% lower (1.01x), and p99 was 3.05% lower (1.03x). These small and mixed single-request differences do not establish a meaningful sequential speedup. A cold miss was slower because it reads PostgreSQL and writes the cache.

### Controlled load (25 VUs, 30 seconds, 3 repetitions per scenario)

| Scenario | Median requests/s | Median p50 | Median p95 | Median p99 | Errors |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PostgreSQL bypass | 371.197 | 63.198 ms | 106.148 ms | 135.131 ms | 0% |
| Redis hit | 437.897 | 52.459 ms | 86.557 ms | 108.572 ms | 0% |

Using the same percentile from each scenario, latency reduction was 16.99% at p50 (1.205x), 18.46% at p95 (1.226x), and 19.65% at p99 (1.245x). Median throughput was 17.97% higher, or 66.700 requests/s more. Throughput is a separate measurement from latency reduction. The three-run ranges were 61.090–63.344 ms vs 51.905–52.840 ms at p50, 99.021–108.283 ms vs 85.703–86.796 ms at p95, and 123.605–136.377 ms vs 108.153–109.300 ms at p99 (bypass vs Redis).

The API logs contained 12,063 / 11,571 / 11,471 `Services` SELECTs in the three bypass runs, and 1 / 0 / 0 in the Redis runs. The one Redis SELECT was the initial cache-populating read; subsequent requests in the measured hit run were served from cache. These are query-event counts from this one-key local test, not a measurement of PostgreSQL CPU, I/O, or production load. Redis GET logs separately recorded a median around 2–3 ms in the sequential samples, with occasional much larger outliers; they do not include JSON deserialization, and SET duration is not separately instrumented. The API logs and k6 console logs remain in the original machine's temporary directory and are not part of this repository; therefore the database query counts and Redis-operation timings are not independently reviewable from the checked-in CSVs.

### Limits on interpretation

The load runs were executed in A-then-C order rather than interleaved, on a single local environment with a tiny fixed data set. This leaves possible time/order effects and says nothing about production hardware or capacity. The test does not demonstrate a number of supported users. Repeat with alternating A/C runs, capture machine and Docker resource limits, and test representative data before using the result as a broader performance claim. The source CSVs and per-run summaries are in `tests/OpsFlow.LoadTests/results/2026-10-14/`. Original API and k6 logs remain in `%TEMP%\OpsFlowRedisBenchmark` on the machine that ran the benchmark and are not committed.

## Cleanup

After copying any desired result files from `%TEMP%`, verify the Compose project identity and then remove only the disposable benchmark stack and its database volume:

```powershell
docker compose -p opsflow-redis-benchmark -f docker-compose.redis-benchmark.yml ps -a
docker compose -p opsflow-redis-benchmark -f docker-compose.redis-benchmark.yml down --volumes --remove-orphans
```

The project name is deliberately different from `opsflow`; never omit it or substitute the development Compose file in the cleanup command.

import http from 'k6/http';
import { check } from 'k6';
import { sha256 } from 'k6/crypto';
import encoding from 'k6/encoding';
import { Counter, Rate, Trend } from 'k6/metrics';

const baseUrl = (__ENV.BASE_URL || 'http://host.docker.internal:5183').replace(/\/$/, '');
const cacheMode = (__ENV.CACHE_MODE || 'Redis').toLowerCase();
const email = __ENV.ADMIN_EMAIL || 'admin@acmetech.io';
const password = [REDACTED] || '[REDACTED DEVELOPMENT CREDENTIAL]';
const vus = Number(__ENV.VUS || 25);
const duration = __ENV.DURATION || '60s';
const servicesRequests = new Counter('services_requests');
const servicesSuccessRate = new Rate('services_success_rate');
const servicesLatency = new Trend('services_latency', true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    services_browse: {
      executor: 'constant-vus',
      exec: 'getServices',
      vus,
      duration,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    services_success_rate: ['rate>0.99'],
    checks: ['rate>0.99'],
  },
  summaryTrendStats: ['avg', 'min', 'med', 'max', 'p(50)', 'p(90)', 'p(95)', 'p(99)'],
};

export function setup() {
  const login = http.post(`${baseUrl}/api/auth/login`, JSON.stringify({ email, password }), {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
  check(login, { 'benchmark admin login succeeds': (response) => response.status === 200 });
  if (login.status !== 200) throw new Error(`Admin login failed (${login.status}): ${login.body}`);

  const accessToken = login.json('accessToken');
  const tokenPayload = JSON.parse(encodingDecode(accessToken.split('.')[1]));
  const organizationId = tokenPayload.orgId;
  const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` };
  const warm = http.get(`${baseUrl}/api/organizations/${organizationId}/services`, { headers });
  check(warm, { 'setup service-list request succeeds': (response) => response.status === 200 });
  if (warm.status !== 200) throw new Error(`Service setup request failed (${warm.status}): ${warm.body}`);

  return {
    accessToken,
    organizationId,
    expectedBodyHash: sha256(warm.body, 'hex'),
  };
}

export function getServices(data) {
  const response = http.get(`${baseUrl}/api/organizations/${data.organizationId}/services`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${data.accessToken}` },
    tags: { operation: 'organization_services', cache_mode: cacheMode },
  });
  servicesRequests.add(1);
  servicesSuccessRate.add(response.status === 200);
  servicesLatency.add(response.timings.duration);
  check(response, {
    'GET services returns 200': (result) => result.status === 200,
    'GET services returns the setup payload': (result) => sha256(result.body, 'hex') === data.expectedBodyHash,
  });
}

export function handleSummary(data) {
  const safeSummary = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(data));
  if (safeSummary.setup_data) delete safeSummary.setup_data.accessToken;
  const path = `/results/${__ENV.RUN_NAME || 'redis-ab-summary'}.json`;
  return {
    stdout: `Benchmark summary saved to ${path}; bearer token removed from exported data.\n`,
    [path]: JSON.stringify(safeSummary, null, 2),
  };
}

function encodingDecode(value) {
  const normalized = value.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
  const padded = normalized + '='.repeat((4 - (normalized.length % 4)) % 4);
  return encoding.b64decode(padded, 'std', 's');
}

الملف كاملًا؛ القيم السرية محجوبة
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [int]$Vus = 25,
    [string]$Duration = "30s",
    [int]$Repetitions = 3,
    [string]$ComposeProject = "opsflow-redis-benchmark",
    [string]$BaseUrl = "http://127.0.0.1:5183",
    [string]$AdminEmail = "admin@acmetech.io",
    [string]$AdminPassword = "[REDACTED DEVELOPMENT CREDENTIAL]"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$repoRoot = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "../..")).Path
$hostProject = Join-Path $repoRoot "tests/OpsFlow.RedisBenchmarkHost/OpsFlow.RedisBenchmarkHost.csproj"
$hostDll = Join-Path $repoRoot "tests/OpsFlow.RedisBenchmarkHost/bin/Release/net8.0/OpsFlow.RedisBenchmarkHost.dll"
$loadScriptDirectory = $PSScriptRoot
$composeFile = Join-Path $repoRoot "docker-compose.redis-benchmark.yml"
$runId = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss"
$outputDirectory = Join-Path $env:TEMP "OpsFlowRedisBenchmark/k6-$runId"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outputDirectory | Out-Null

dotnet build $hostProject --configuration Release --no-restore
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Benchmark host build failed." }

$runningServices = & docker compose -p $ComposeProject -f $composeFile ps --status running --services
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or @($runningServices) -notcontains "postgres" -or @($runningServices) -notcontains "redis") {
    throw "Start the isolated benchmark dependencies first using the command in README.redis-ab.md."
}

$previousEnvironment = @{}
foreach ($name in @(
    "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT", "ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection", "Redis__ConnectionString",
    "JwtSettings__SecretKey", "JwtSettings__Issuer", "JwtSettings__Audience",
    "JwtSettings__AccessTokenExpirationMinutes", "JwtSettings__RefreshTokenExpirationDays",
    "Benchmark__CacheMode", "CACHE_MODE", "BASE_URL", "VUS", "DURATION", "ADMIN_EMAIL", "ADMIN_PASSWORD"
)) {
    $previousEnvironment[$name] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($name, "Process")
}

$env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = "Development"
$env:ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection = "Host=127.0.0.1;Port=15433;Database=opsflow_redis_benchmark;Username=opsflow_benchmark;Password=[REDACTED];"
$env:Redis__ConnectionString = "127.0.0.1:16380"
$env:JwtSettings__SecretKey = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::GetBytes(48))
$env:JwtSettings__Issuer = "OpsFlow"
$env:JwtSettings__Audience = "OpsFlowClients"
$env:JwtSettings__AccessTokenExpirationMinutes = "60"
$env:JwtSettings__RefreshTokenExpirationDays = "7"
$env:BASE_URL = "http://host.docker.internal:5183"
$env:VUS = [string]$Vus
$env:DURATION = $Duration
$env:ADMIN_EMAIL = $AdminEmail
$env:ADMIN_PASSWORD = [REDACTED]

$http = [System.Net.Http.HttpClient]::new()
$http.Timeout = [TimeSpan]::FromSeconds(5)
$baseUri = [Uri]::new($BaseUrl.TrimEnd('/') + '/')
$results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()

function Start-HostForMode {
    param([ValidateSet("Bypass", "Redis")][string]$Mode, [string]$LogPrefix)
    $env:Benchmark__CacheMode = $Mode
    $process = Start-Process -FilePath "dotnet" `
        -ArgumentList @($hostDll, "--urls", $BaseUrl) `
        -WorkingDirectory $repoRoot -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -RedirectStandardOutput "$LogPrefix.api.stdout.log" `
        -RedirectStandardError "$LogPrefix.api.stderr.log"

    for ($attempt = 0; $attempt -lt 90; $attempt++) {
        if ($process.HasExited) { throw "Benchmark API exited during startup; inspect $LogPrefix.api.stderr.log." }
        try {
            $response = $http.GetAsync([Uri]::new($baseUri, "api/health")).GetAwaiter().GetResult()
            if ([int]$response.StatusCode -eq 200) { $response.Dispose(); return $process }
            $response.Dispose()
        } catch { }
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500
    }
    throw "Benchmark API health endpoint did not respond; inspect $LogPrefix.api.stdout.log."
}

function Stop-Host {
    param([System.Diagnostics.Process]$Process)
    if (-not $Process.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $Process.Id -Force; $Process.WaitForExit() }
    $Process.Dispose()
}

function Invoke-K6 {
    param([string]$Mode, [int]$Repetition)

    $runName = "$($Mode.ToLowerInvariant())-run$Repetition"
    $summaryPath = Join-Path $outputDirectory "$runName.json"
    $logPrefix = Join-Path $outputDirectory $runName
    $api = Start-HostForMode -Mode $Mode -LogPrefix $logPrefix
    try {
        $env:CACHE_MODE = $Mode
        $dockerArgs = @(
            "run", "--rm", "--add-host", "host.docker.internal:host-gateway",
            "--mount", "type=bind,source=$loadScriptDirectory,target=/scripts,readonly",
            "--mount", "type=bind,source=$outputDirectory,target=/results",
            "-e", "CACHE_MODE", "-e", "BASE_URL", "-e", "VUS", "-e", "DURATION", "-e", "ADMIN_EMAIL", "-e", "ADMIN_PASSWORD", "-e", "RUN_NAME=$runName",
            "grafana/k6:latest", "run", "/scripts/redis-ab-load.js"
        )
        & docker @dockerArgs 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath "$logPrefix.k6.log"
        $dockerExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
        if (-not (Test-Path $summaryPath)) { throw "k6 did not write $summaryPath. Check $logPrefix.k6.log." }
        if ($dockerExitCode -ne 0) { throw "k6 returned exit code $dockerExitCode. The summary is preserved at $summaryPath." }

        $summary = Get-Content $summaryPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
        $requestValues = $summary.metrics.services_requests.values
        $latency = $summary.metrics.services_latency.values
        $requestCount = [int]$requestValues.PSObject.Properties["count"].Value
        $requestRate = [double]$requestValues.PSObject.Properties["rate"].Value
        $p50 = [double]$latency.PSObject.Properties["p(50)"].Value
        $p95 = [double]$latency.PSObject.Properties["p(95)"].Value
        $p99 = [double]$latency.PSObject.Properties["p(99)"].Value
        $successRate = [double]$summary.metrics.services_success_rate.values.rate
        $logText = Get-Content "$logPrefix.api.stdout.log" -Raw
        $pathEvents = if ($Mode -eq "Bypass") {
            [regex]::Matches($logText, "Benchmark cache BYPASS for key services:org:").Count
        } else {
            [regex]::Matches($logText, "Cache HIT for key services:org:").Count
        }
        if ($pathEvents -lt $requestCount) {
            throw "$Mode path verification failed: k6 measured $requestCount service requests but only $pathEvents matching cache logs were captured."
        }

        $results.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Scenario = $Mode
            Repetition = $Repetition
            VUs = $Vus
            Duration = $Duration
            Requests = $requestCount
            RequestsPerSecond = [Math]::Round($requestRate, 3)
            ErrorsPercent = [Math]::Round((1 - $successRate) * 100, 4)
            P50Ms = [Math]::Round($p50, 3)
            P95Ms = [Math]::Round($p95, 3)
            P99Ms = [Math]::Round($p99, 3)
            VerifiedPathEvents = $pathEvents
            SummaryJson = $summaryPath
            ApiLog = "$logPrefix.api.stdout.log"
            K6Log = "$logPrefix.k6.log"
        })
        Write-Host "$Mode k6 run ${Repetition}: requests=$requestCount, RPS=$([Math]::Round($requestRate, 2)), errors=$([Math]::Round((1 - $successRate) * 100, 3))%, p50=$([Math]::Round($p50, 2)) ms, p95=$([Math]::Round($p95, 2)) ms, p99=$([Math]::Round($p99, 2)) ms; path events=$pathEvents."
    }
    finally {
        Stop-Host -Process $api
    }
}

try {
    foreach ($mode in @("Bypass", "Redis")) {
        for ($repetition = 1; $repetition -le $Repetitions; $repetition++) {
            Invoke-K6 -Mode $mode -Repetition $repetition
        }
    }
    $summaryCsv = Join-Path $outputDirectory "load-summary.csv"
    $results | Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation -Path $summaryCsv
    Write-Host "Load results: $summaryCsv"
    Write-Host "Detailed JSON and API/k6 logs: $outputDirectory"
}
finally {
    $http.Dispose()
    foreach ($name in $previousEnvironment.Keys) {
        if ($null -eq $previousEnvironment[$name]) {
            [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($name, $null, "Process")
        } else {
            [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($name, $previousEnvironment[$name], "Process")
        }
    }
}
